description: A thin spirit varnish rubbed sparingly over polished leather as a protective finish. Cockerell warns that thick or excess varnish browns with age, dulls the gold, and makes the surface brittle at the joints.
name: varnish

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1901), Chapter XIV, p.193. Internet Archive.
